text: So here it is, on the scene you watched. Secretion: beta cells release insulin, a ligand, by exocytosis. Transport: the blood carries it widely, and it reaches cells through tissue fluid. Binding: on target cells, it binds to cell surface receptors whose binding sites are complementary in shape. That binding starts a specific response: muscle cells take up more glucose. Cells that share the receptor can all respond; cells without it do not.
